transcription: Stubborn Old Historical Lady Polaxic Story. So, first a few pieces of background info one. I've been unemployed for some time now, and go to library a lot. I've gotten to know most of the librarians by name, and a handful of them know I'm a Polish immigrant Brooklyn, NYC. I came here at 11, and 38, my English fluency is higher than a native speaker with just a hint of an accent. My Polish fluency is almost of a native speaker with a hint of an accent. 2. The term I used in the title, is a deregatory term for Polish immigrants who move to the US and absolutely fail to assimilate. Decades in the country, cannot communicate in English at all, only interact with other Polish immigrants. So, story around 130-2008 lunch, start watching a YouTube channel, and dose off. Librarian Lisa shakes me to wake me up and seems distressed. She says, I need your help, my first thought is that someone is being violent and the one librarian who knows how to handle himself isn't there. No. There is an 80-year-old Polish lady sitting at a table over, crying and saying stuff in Polish hysterically. Lisa can only figure out she's Polish and needs help with documents. I walk over, and while I'm calming her down, it turns out she needs help filling out an international wire transfer form by 5pm bank holiday tomorrow to transfer a 100,000 used to a Polish bank account because on Tuesday she is moving back to Poland. Okay. I can help. It's 230, she's a moron for doing it last second, but whatever. Problem I recently developed carpal tunnel syndrome in my dominant hand. The only way my hand writing is legible is if my font size is like 1 inch. So I tell her I will tell her what to write. Nope, her hands are shaky and she doesn't want to write either. Fine, I ask Lisa if any of the high school or college kids who volunteer there are around. Luckily Eric was around. So it becomes a three-way communication thing. I explained to her what everything is, tell Eric what to write. Thank the god she had a printout of a previous wire transfer someone did for her, otherwise we would still be there six hours later. She's a crotchety, complainy old person type, and any information she has as scribbled in a tiny notebook had to use white out twice for her contacts phone number in Poland. Almost an hour later we are done. She gives Eric 4 probably because he was Chinese American and gives me a 10. Cool. Here is where the real-old person stubbornness comes into play. I say, cool we are done. I'm happy to go with you to the bank to make sure everything is okay. All I ask is you pay my car service fair back. My feet hurt and it's hot out. I'm not going to tire myself walking 10 blocks back from the bank. Her answer? No. I want to go to the location that is near my house because people there are nice to me. I try to reason, it is 3.30, bank closes at 5. Her location is in the middle of another burrow that we have to cross a bridge to get to, and holiday rush hour just started. Also, how the F does she know if people are nice to where she speaks all of 10 words in English. She dose not budge. Fine. If she pays my cab fare back, I'll waste 45 minutes each way, however long at the bank, to help out. There's a car service dispatch right across the street. I tell her to start getting her crud ready and I'll arrange the cab. I go, they confirm it, and say it will be $42. Fair price given the circumstances 45 minute trip. I walk back to the library she's standing outside, how much is it going to be? 42. I'm not paying that, they're ripping me off I paid 10 less to get here, no crud old lady. You used a different car service, and you came late morning after rush hour when it's a 30 and not 45 minute trip. Once again, I try to reason with her we have 1.30 to get this done before banks close for the holiday. No. No way in hell are they gonna rip her off by charging that much that was it. I said I had done as much as I could
